topics.name: The SK model and Parisi functional
topics.description: The spin energy, cumulative order parameter, value function, and auxiliary diffusion define the problem.

topics.name: Full support and variational conditions
topics.description: Minimality relates the consistency function to the support of the order-parameter measure.

topics.name: Excluding gaps in the support
topics.description: Curvature and endpoint conditions rule out intervals with no mass.

topics.name: Heat equations and shape inequalities
topics.description: The forward and backward equations supply the signs needed by the integral estimate.

topics.name: The rational identity and coercive inequality
topics.description: An exact polynomial identity and a vanishing integral leave a positive lower bound.

topics.name: Smoothness and positive density
topics.description: A bound at a fixed time combines with the minimiser identities to control the derivative of the order parameter.

topics.name: Ground-state energy and Gaussian approximation
topics.description: Martingale moments express the energy and allow approximation by finitely many Gaussian variables.

topics.name: QAOA and optimisation consequences
topics.description: Full support supplies inputs to classical optimisation and the separate construction of near-optimal quantum circuits.

about.heading: What this reader is
paragraphs: This reader holds three papers on one theorem about the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass, from OpenAI’s mathematics release, with OpenAI’s proof beside the text. That proof is written in Lean, a programming language whose compiler rejects a proof with a wrong step. You read a paper as you would any paper. Each phrase that a Lean declaration states is underlined in the colour of its topic, and clicking it opens that Lean with a plain title, whether the Lean states the same as the phrase, more or less, and a reading note drafted by an AI agent.

There are three papers on the result. The exposition has the ideas, with worked examples. The short paper has the result and its proof, for readers who know the field. The long record has each step of the argument with the source it comes from.

Each step of the argument is one entry in a graph: a claim, an assumption, or a declaration in Lean. Links between steps say which steps the argument for a result uses. Statements in the three papers are tied to the steps they state, explain or use. An AI agent read each statement and its Lean and linked them. No independent mathematician has reviewed these links, and no program tests whether the two say the same thing. The reader adds layout and wording; it says what was recorded and no more.

about.heading: The architectural companion
paragraphs: A longer paper, written for this project, on why the result is written up as three papers linked to one set of steps, and on how those steps and links are made.

about.heading: Who made this reader
paragraphs: Will Cook made this reader with AI agents, which wrote its code, its steps and its ties under his direction. The proof and its Lean are OpenAI’s. Hong-Bin Chen first proved full support in a July 2026 paper, and the earlier results are credited in the papers.

The reader belongs to Plectis, Will Cook’s projects on researching mathematics with AI and on tools that help people follow what AI produces. His own research is on Erdős problems, questions posed by the mathematician Paul Erdős. On Plectis Atlas, the results in OpenAI’s mathematics release are set beside the outside reports that assess them, and family 281, the result explained here, has its own page.

folderWords.ComparatorChallenges: The definitions and the two main statements copied out alone, with sorry in place of each proof, as challenge files for a Comparator run.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport: The definitions of the model and the final full support theorem.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Backward: Solutions of the backward equation: their shape, comparison, gradient bounds and what happens on a terminal plateau.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Control: The control problem behind the value function: payoffs, grid approximations, and the value's Lipschitz and convexity properties.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Density: Densities on finite grids, Gaussian tails and the ratio comparisons that give coercivity.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Diffusion: The diffusion driven by the gradient: its construction by Picard iteration, feedback verification and uniqueness.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Foundations: Groundwork used throughout: the cascade, semigroups, variance heat curves, step data and finite values.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Moments: The square moment and curvature moment along the diffusion, and the equations they satisfy.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Parabolic: Comparison principles for parabolic inequalities, and Burgers, forward and tilted evolutions.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Regularity: Smoothness of the value function: its derivatives, their bounds and their limits.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKSupport/Support: The final argument: contact, the variational inequality and the exclusion of gaps.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue: The definitions and the main statement of the ground-state value result.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Coercivity: Coercivity estimates, pointwise and integrated, including the zero-gap case.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Control: Controls and verification for the value: progressive controls, stability and regularity on strips.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Equations: Estimates for the equations: comparison principles, polynomial moments, forced generators and strip bounds.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Evolution: The Parisi evolution: Cole-Hopf, heat kernel bounds, grid convergence and assembly of the Parisi value.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Gaussian: Gaussian building blocks: Brownian coordinates, density derivatives and split profile estimates.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/GroundState: The passage to the ground state: Guerra bounds, tree and cascade laws, Gumbel maxima and rounding to spins.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Processes: Diffusion processes for the value: existence, Euler meshes, martingale facts and gradient isometries.
folderWords.OAI/Probability/SKValue/Variation: First variations, contact at a minimiser and the ground-state value derived from contact.

words.checksTerms: OpenAI’s proof is written in Lean, a programming language whose compiler rejects a proof with a wrong step. Comparator is a program that compares a Lean proof with a separately written statement. An extraction is a program run inside Lean that lists what a compiled theorem uses and which axioms it depends on. The main theorem here is the full-support theorem for the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass. A step is one claim, assumption or Lean declaration in its argument, a tie joins a statement in a paper to a step, and a run record says what ran or was planned and with what outcome.
